title: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Mustard Cream Sauce
description: Pan-Seared Pork Chops with Mustard Cream Sauce is a classic Continental main course featuring juicy, golden-brown pork chops served with a rich Dijon mustard cream sauce. Paired with buttery mashed potatoes and seasonal vegetables, it is a comforting yet elegant dish.

ingredients.title: For the Pork Chops
items: Bone-in pork chops (about 200–250 g each, 2.5 cm thick) – 4
Freshly ground black pepper – to taste
Fresh rosemary or thyme – 1 sprig (optional, for aroma)

ingredients.title: For the Mustard Cream Sauce
items: Dry white wine (e.g., Sauvignon Blanc) – 120 ml

instruction.title: Step 1 – Prepare the Pork Chops
steps: Pat pork chops dry with paper towels (important for browning).
Season generously with salt and pepper on both sides.

instruction.title: Step 2 – Sear the Pork
steps: Heat olive oil and butter in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering.
Add pork chops and sear 3–4 minutes per side, until golden brown and the internal temperature reaches 63°C (145°F).
In the last minute, add rosemary or thyme for fragrance, basting chops with the butter.
Transfer pork to a warm plate and cover loosely with foil to rest.

instruction.title: Step 3 – Make the Sauce
steps: Discard excess fat from the skillet, leaving about 1 tsp.
Add butter and sauté shallots over medium heat until soft (about 1–2 minutes).
Deglaze with white wine, scraping up browned bits; reduce by half.
Stir in chicken stock and reduce slightly.
Lower heat, add cream, and simmer gently until the sauce thickens to coat a spoon.
Whisk in Dijon mustard (and whole-grain mustard if using).

instruction.title: Step 4 – Serve
steps: Return pork chops to the skillet briefly to coat with sauce, or plate chops and spoon sauce over them.
Serve with buttery mashed potatoes, steamed green beans, or sautéed spinach.

servingSuggestions.title: Serving Suggestions
items: Serve with buttery mashed potatoes or pomme purée.
Pair with steamed green beans or sautéed spinach.
Enjoy with a glass of dry white wine such as Sauvignon Blanc.

chefTips: Pat the pork chops dry before searing for a perfect golden crust.
Allow the pork to rest for a few minutes after cooking to retain its juices.
For deeper flavor, brine pork chops in a 5% salt solution (50 g salt per liter of water) for 2–4 hours before cooking. Pat dry before searing.
Do not boil the cream sauce after adding the mustard to maintain its smooth texture.
